options: A. Leave metal garden rakes and hoes lying face-up in tall grass with the sharp tines pointing skyward so you can spot them easily.

D. Mix double the recommended concentration of garden pesticide in an unlabeled drinking cup and spray it upwind on a gusty afternoon.

B. 100 percent germination rate, because unsprouted seeds do not count
C. 41 percent germination rate, because you must divide the sprouted total in half
D. 82 percent germination rate, with failures likely due to seed age, storage conditions, or moisture levels
choices: A. 18 percent germination rate, caused by excessive moonlight
B. 100 percent germination rate, because unsprouted seeds do not count
C. 41 percent germination rate, because you must divide the sprouted total in half

quiz_item.correct_answer: D. 82 percent germination rate, with failures likely due to seed age, storage conditions, or moisture levels
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): When 82 of 100 tested seeds sprout, the germination rate is 82 percent, and non-germinating seeds typically fail due to age, damaged embryos, or improper moisture and warmth (p. 72).

pamphlet_excerpts: Ancient Human Bee Partnership: You may have never thought much about honey bees, but there has been a strong relationship between bees and humans for thousands of years (p. 59).
Pollinator Importance for Food: Without these winged creatures, many of our food sources would be in great peril (p. 59).
Crop and Feed Pollination: We rely on honeybees not only for the sweet honey they make, but more importantly for their ability to pollinate many of the crops and livestock feed (p. 59).
Cross Pollination for Seeds: Some plants can produce seeds only if pollen is exchanged between flowers on the same plant, or from flowers of different plants from the same variety (p. 59).

Step 3 - Identify Diverse Native Pollinators: Birds, bats, bumblebees, butterflies, and many other creatures help transfer pollen as they flit from flower to flower or feed on the nectar (p. 59).
Step 4 - Compare Honeybee Pollination Advantages: Honey bees, however, have three advantages over all of these other pollinators (p. 59).

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following and record weekly observations. Discuss the results of your project with your counselor. (a) Build a compost bin and maintain it for 90 days. (b) Build a vermicompost bin (worm compost bin) and maintain it for 90 days. (c) Build a hydroponic garden containing three vegetables or herbs, or three ornamental plants. Maintain this garden through harvest or flowering, or for 90 days. (d) Build one water garden, either in a container (at least 12 by 6 inches and 6 inches deep), or in the ground as a small, decorative pond no larger than 6 by 3 feet and 24 inches deep. Maintain the water garden for 90 days. (e) Prepare a honey super for use on a hive or colony. Remove a filled honey super from the hive or colony and prepare the honey for sale. (f) Grow a garden of your own using soil from seed or plantings to harvest or for 90 days, whichever is earlier. This can be an outdoor garden or indoors using appropriate containers, and should include at least three types of plants approved by your counselor.
